Scene 02

FBI Headquarters · Washington, D.C.

Dana Scully

Agent Dana Scully.

Scott Blevins

Come in. Thank you for coming on such short notice. Please... You've been with us just over two years.

Dana Scully

Yes, sir.

Scott Blevins

You went to medical school, but you chose not to practice. How did you come to work for the FBI?

Dana Scully

Well, sir, I was recruited out of medical school. My parents still think it was an act of rebellion but I saw the FBI as a place where I could distinguish myself.

FBI Official

Are you familiar with an agent named Fox Mulder?

Dana Scully

Yes, I am.

FBI Official

How so?

Dana Scully

By reputation. He's an Oxford-educated psychologist who wrote a monograph on serial killers and the occult that helped catch Monty Propps in 1988. Generally thought of as the best analyst in the violent crime section. He had a nickname at the academy: "spooky" Mulder.

Scott Blevins

I'll also tell you that agent Mulder has developed a consuming devotion to an unassigned project. Are you familiar with the so-called X-Files?

Dana Scully

I believe they have to do with unexplained phenomena.

Scott Blevins

We want you to assist Mulder. You will write field reports on your activities along with your observations on the validity of the work.

Dana Scully

You want me to debunk the X-Files project?

Scott Blevins

We trust you'll make the proper analysis. You'll want to contact agent Mulder shortly. We look forward to seeing your reports.

Fox Mulder

Sorry, nobody down here but the FBI's most unwanted.

Dana Scully

Agent Mulder. I'm Dana Scully. I've been assigned to work with you.

Fox Mulder

Isn't it nice to be so highly regarded? Who did you tick off to get stuck with this detail?

Dana Scully

Actually, I'm looking forward to working with you.

Fox Mulder

I was under the impression that you were sent to spy on me.

Dana Scully

If you have any doubt about my qualifications...

Fox Mulder

You're a medical doctor. You teach at the academy. You did your undergraduate degree in physics. "Einstein's twin paradox: a new interpretation." Dana Scully's senior thesis. Now that's a credential, rewriting Einstein.

Dana Scully

Did you read it?

Fox Mulder

I did. I liked it. In most of my work the laws of physics rarely seem to apply. Maybe I can get your medical opinion on this. Oregon female, age 21. No explainable cause of death. Autopsy shows nothing. Zip. There are, however, these two distinct marks on her lower back. Dr. Scully, can you ID these marks?

Dana Scully

Needle punctures, maybe. An animal bite, electrocution.

Fox Mulder

How's your chemistry? This is the substance found in the surrounding tissue.

Dana Scully

It's organic. I don't know. Is it some kind of synthetic protein?

Fox Mulder

Beats me. I've never seen it, either but here it is again in South Dakota, and again in Texas.

Dana Scully

Do you have a theory?

Fox Mulder

I have plenty of theories but maybe what you can explain to me is why it's bureau policy to label these cases "unexplained phenomena" and ignore them. Do you believe in the existence of extraterrestrials?

Dana Scully

Logically, I would have to say no given the distances needed to travel from the far reaches of space the energy requirements would exceed a spacecraft's capabilities.

Fox Mulder

Conventional wisdom. This Oregon female-- she's the fourth person in her graduating class to die under mysterious circumstances. When convention and science offer us no answers might we not finally turn to the fantastic as a plausibility?

Dana Scully

The girl obviously died of something. If it was natural causes, it's plausible there was something missed in the postmortem. If she was murdered it's plausible there was a sloppy investigation. What I find fantastic is any notion that there are answers beyond the realm of science. The answers are there. You have to know where to look.

Fox Mulder

That's why they put the "I" in FBI see you tomorrow morning, Scully, bright and early. We leave for the very plausible state of Oregon at 8:00 a.m.

Scene 03

Airplane to Oregon

Airline Pilot

I'd like to ask all passengers to fasten their seat belts as we're about to make our descent...

Fox Mulder

This must be the place.

Scene 04

Bellefleur, Oregon

Dana Scully

You didn't mention yesterday this case has already been investigated.

Fox Mulder

Yeah, the FBI got involved after the first three deaths when local authorities failed to turn up any evidence. Our boys came out here, spent a week enjoyed the local salmon-- which is just to die for, if you pardon the expression. Without explanation, they were called back in. The case was reclassified and buried in the X-Files until I dug it up last week.

Dana Scully

And you found something they didn't? The autopsy reports of the first three victims show no unidentified marks or tissue samples but those reports were signed by a different medical examiner than the latest victim.

Fox Mulder

That's pretty good, Scully.

Dana Scully

Better than you expected, or better than you hoped?

Fox Mulder

Well, I'll let you know when we get past the easy part.

Dana Scully

Is the medical examiner a suspect?

Fox Mulder

We won't know until we do some grave digging. I've arranged to exhume one of the other victims to see if we can get a tissue sample to match the girl's. You're not squeamish, are you?

Dana Scully

I've never had the pleasure.

(indistinct radio)

(audio feedback)

Dana Scully

What's going on? What the hell was that about?

Fox Mulder

Oh, you know... Probably nothing.

Coastal Northwest Oregon · March 7, 1992

John Truitt

Mr. Mulder, county coroner's office.

Fox Mulder

Yeah, hi. This is agent Scully. How soon can we get started?

John Truitt

We're ready to go.

Fox Mulder

Were you able to arrange for an examination facility?

Dr. Jay Nemman

Excuse me. Excuse me. No. Please stay in... I don't know who you people think you are. You think you can come up here and do whatever you damn please, don't you?

Fox Mulder

I'm sorry. You are..?

Dr. Jay Nemman

Jay Nemman, county medical examiner.

Fox Mulder

Surely, you must have been informed.

Dr. Jay Nemman

No. No, we've been away.

Fox Mulder

Well, that answers a question we had: why you hadn't done the recent autopsy. You're aware of the tissue sample that was taken from her body.

Dr. Jay Nemman

What is the insinuation here? Are you saying I missed something in those kids' exams?

Dana Scully

We're not insinuating anything, sir.

Dr. Jay Nemman

Wait a minute! Well, I think you are. If you're making an accusation you'd better have something to back it up.

Theresa Nemman

Daddy, please, let's just go home. Let's go home, please!

Fox Mulder

Guy obviously needed a longer vacation.

Dana Scully

Ray Soames was the third victim. After graduating high school he spent time in a state mental hospital. Treated for post-adolescent schizophrenia.

Fox Mulder

Soames confessed to the first two murders. He pleaded to be locked up but he couldn't produce any evidence that he committed the crimes. Did you read the cause of death?

Dana Scully

Exposure. His body was found in the woods after escaping the hospital.

Fox Mulder

Missing for only seven hours in July. How does a 20-year-old die of exposure on a warm, summer night in Oregon?

John Truitt

This isn't official procedure.

Fox Mulder

Really? It's probably a safe bet Ray Soames never made the varsity basketball team. Seal this up right now. Nobody sees or touches this. Nobody.

Scene 06

Examination Facility · 10:56 P.M.

Fox Mulder

This is amazing, Scully. Do you know what this could mean? It's almost too big to even comprehend.

Dana Scully

The subject is 156 centimeters in length weighing 52 pounds in extremis. Corpse is in advanced stages of decay and desiccation. Distinguishing features include large ocular cavities oblique cranium-- indicates subject is not human. Could you point that flash away from me?

Fox Mulder

If it's not human, what is it?

Dana Scully

It's mammalian. It's a chimpanzee or something from the ape family possibly an orangutan.

Fox Mulder

Buried in the city cemetery in Ray's grave? Try telling that to the good townsfolk or to Ray's family. I want tissue samples, x rays, blood typing, toxicology and a full genetic work-up. What we can't do here, we'll order to go.

Dana Scully

You don't honestly believe this is an extraterrestrial? This is somebody's sick joke.

Fox Mulder

Is there any reason we can't do those x rays right now? I'm not crazy, Scully. I have the same doubts you do.

Scully's Hotel Room

Dana Scully

Visual laboratory inspection of the body and x-Ray analysis

Dana Scully (recorded)

Confirms homologous, but possibly mutated, mammalian physiology. However, does not account for small, unidentified object found in subject's nasal cavity. A grey, metallic implant forming...

Who is it?

Fox Mulder

Steven spielberg. I'm going for a run. Want to come?

Dana Scully

Pass.

Figure out what that little thing is?

Dana Scully

No. And I'm not losing any sleep over it. Good night.

Scene 08

Raymon County State Psychiatric Hospital

Dr. Glass

Ray Soames was a patient of mine. I oversaw his treatment for over a year for clinical schizophrenia. Ray had an inability to grasp reality. He seemed to suffer from some kind of post-traumatic stress.

Fox Mulder

Is that something you've seen before?

Dr. Glass

I've treated similar cases.

Dana Scully

Were any of those Ray Soames' classmates?

Dr. Glass

Yes.

Fox Mulder

We're trying to find a connection in these deaths. Did you treat any of these kids with hypnosis?

Dr. Glass

No. I did not.

Dana Scully

Are you treating any of these kids now?

Dr. Glass

Currently? Yes, I'm treating Billy Miles and Peggy O'Dell.

Dana Scully

They're here at this hospital?

Dr. Glass

Going on four years now.

Dana Scully

Would it be possible to talk to them?

Dr. Glass

Well, you might find it difficult. Certainly in Billy Miles' case. Billy's experiencing what we call a waking coma. Functionally, his brain waves are flat.

Dana Scully

How did it happen?

Dr. Glass

He and Peggy were involved in an automobile accident. Peggy? We have some visitors. Would you talk with them?

Peggy O'Dell

Billy wants me to read now.

Fox Mulder

Does he like it when you read to him?

Peggy O'Dell

Yes.

Fox Mulder

Doctor I'm wondering if we can do a cursory medical exam on Peggy?

(crashing, yelling)

Nurse

Peggy, what are you doing?

Dr. Glass

No one will hurt you.

(screaming)

Dr. Glass

Get an orderly! Get an orderly! Nobody's going to hurt you.

(screaming)

Peggy O'Dell

Stop it!

Dr. Glass

It's all right.

Nurse

Honey, you're going to be fine. Calm down. You know that you will be all right.

Fox Mulder

Billy said he was sorry he didn't get to say good-bye.

Dana Scully

How did you know she would have the marks?

Fox Mulder

I don't know. Lucky guess?

Dana Scully

Damn it, Mulder, cut the crap. What is going on here? What do you know about those marks?

Fox Mulder

I don't think you're ready for what I think.

Dana Scully

I'm here to solve this case. I want the truth.

Fox Mulder

I think those kids have been abducted.

Dana Scully

By who?

Fox Mulder

By what.

Dana Scully

You don't really believe that.

Fox Mulder

Do you have a better explanation?

Dana Scully

I'll buy that girl is suffering some kind of pronounced psychosis. Whether it's organic or the result of those marks I can't say but to say that they've been riding around in flying saucers-- there is nothing to support that.

Fox Mulder

Nothing scientific, you mean.

Dana Scully

There has got to be an explanation. You've got four victims-- all of them died in or near the woods. They found Karen Swenson's body in the forest in her pajamas ten Miles from her house. How did she get there? What were those kids doing out there in the forest?

(mechanical humming)

Scene 09

Collum National Forest · Northwest Oregon

Dana Scully

Mulder?

(mechanical hum increasing)

Dana Scully

Mulder, is that you? Mulder? Special agent Dana Scully, FBI drop your weapon.

Detective Miles

I'm with the county sheriff's department. You're trespassing on private property here.

Dana Scully

We are conducting an investigation.

Detective Miles

Get in your car and leave or I'll have to arrest you. I don't care who you are.

Fox Mulder

This is a crime scene.

Detective Miles

Did you hear what I said? You are on private property without legal permission. Now, I'm only going to say it one more time. Get in your car and leave!

Fox Mulder

What's he doing out here all by himself?

Dana Scully

Maybe it has something to do with this. What do you think it is?

Fox Mulder

I don't know. Is it a campfire?

Dana Scully

It was all over the ground. I think something's going on out here. Some kind of a sacrifice, maybe. What if these kids are involved in some kind of a cult and that man knows something about it? I want to come back here. You okay, Mulder?

Fox Mulder

Yeah. I'm just, uh...

Dana Scully

What are you looking for? What happened?

Fox Mulder

We lost power. Brakes, steering, everything. We lost nine minutes. Whoo!

Dana Scully

We lost what?

Fox Mulder

Nine minutes! I looked at my watch just before the flash and it was 9:03. It just turned 9:13. Look. Look! Oh, yes! Abductees. People that have made UFO sightings. They've reported unexplained time loss.

Dana Scully

Come on.

Fox Mulder

Gone! Just like that.

Dana Scully

No, wait a minute. You're saying that... That time disappeared. Time can't just disappear. It's a universal invariant.

(engine starts)

Fox Mulder

Not in this zip code.

Scully's Hotel Room

Dana Scully

Great.

Scene 11

Mulder's Hotel Room

Fox Mulder

Hi.

Dana Scully

I want you to look at something.

Fox Mulder

Come on in.

Dana Scully

What are they? Mulder, what are they?!

Fox Mulder

Mosquito bites.

Dana Scully

Are you sure?

Fox Mulder

Yeah. I got eaten up a lot myself out there. You okay?

Dana Scully

Yes.

Fox Mulder

You're shaking.

Dana Scully

I need to sit down.

Fox Mulder

Take your time. I was 12 when it happened. My sister was eight. She just disappeared out of her bed one night. Just gone. Vanished. No note, no phone calls, no evidence of anything.

Dana Scully

You never found her.

Fox Mulder

It tore the family apart. No one would talk about it. There were no facts to confront nothing to offer any hope.

Dana Scully

What did you do?

Fox Mulder

Eventually, I went off to school in England. I came back, got recruited by the bureau. Seems I had a natural aptitude for applying behavioral models to criminal cases. My success allowed me a certain freedom to pursue my own interests and that's when I came across the X-Files.

Dana Scully

By accident?

Fox Mulder

At first, it looked like a garbage dump for UFO sightings, alien abduction reports. The kind of stuff that most people laugh at as being ridiculous. But I was fascinated. I read all the cases I could get my hands on. Hundreds of them. I read everything I could about paranormal phenomenon about the occult and... There's classified government information I've been trying to access but someone has been blocking my attempts to get at it.

Dana Scully

Who? I don't understand.

Fox Mulder

Someone at a higher level of power. The only reason I've been allowed to continue is because I've made connections in Congress.

Dana Scully

They're afraid of what? That you'll leak this information?

Fox Mulder

You're part of that agenda, you know that.

Dana Scully

I'm not a part of any agenda. You've got to trust me. I'm here just like you-- to solve this.

Fox Mulder

I'm telling you this, Scully, because you need to know because of what you've seen. In my research I've worked very closely with a man named dr. Heinz Werber. He's taken me through deep hypnosis. I've been able to go into my own repressed memories to the night my sister disappeared. I can recall a bright light outside and a presence in the room. I was paralyzed unable to respond to my sister's calls for help. Listen to me, Scully. This thing exists.

Dana Scully

How do you know?

Fox Mulder

The government knows about it and I got to know what they're protecting. Nothing else matters to me and this is as close as I've ever gotten to it.

(phone ringing)

Fox Mulder

Hello? What? Who is this? Who is th..? That was some woman and she said Peggy O'Dell was dead.

Dana Scully

The girl in the wheelchair?
